svg.title: assign() versus subscribe(): two incompatible ways to read a topic
svg.desc: Two columns. Left, subscribe(): assignment() is empty until the first poll() completes a group-join handshake, partitions are chosen by the group coordinator and can be rebalanced automatically when membership changes, and it gives automatic failover if a consumer dies. Right, assign(): assignment() populates immediately with no group-join needed, the calling code names the exact partition, there is no rebalancing even if a group_id is set for offset tracking, and there is no automatic failover if the process managing an assigned partition dies. A red box at the bottom shows that calling subscribe() on a consumer that already called assign() raises a real IllegalStateError -- the two modes cannot be mixed.
svg.text: Two Modes, Never Both at Once
- assignment() empty until first poll() joins the group
- group coordinator chooses which partitions this consumer gets
- automatic failover -- a dead consumer's partitions get
reassigned to whoever's left, with no outside intervention
Default choice: parallel processing, automatic recovery
- assignment() populated immediately, no group-join at all
- the calling code names the exact partition it wants
- no rebalancing, ever -- even with a group_id set
- group_id (if set) only stores offsets for tracking
- no automatic failover -- a dead process's assigned
partition simply stops being read until restarted
Narrow use: debugging, manual partition control
Calling subscribe() after assign() (or the reverse) raises a real IllegalStateError
"You must choose only one way to configure your consumer" -- a protocol-level constraint, not a library quirk.
